name: Saint Mark the Evangelist
dates: First century · Jerusalem, Rome and Alexandria
history: John Mark, the companion of Paul, Barnabas and Peter, wrote the shortest of the four Gospels, probably the first. Early tradition says he set down the preaching of Peter in Rome. He is held to have founded the Church of Alexandria, and his relics were carried to Venice in 828. His symbol is the lion.
life: The Acts of the Apostles tells us that the first Christians of Jerusalem met in the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark, and that Peter went there when an angel freed him from prison. Mark set out with his cousin Barnabas and with Paul on their first journey, but left them at Perga, and Paul refused to take him again, so that Barnabas and Paul parted. Years later Paul asked for him, ‘for he is useful to me for ministry’, and Peter calls him ‘my son’. Papias, writing early in the second century, says that Mark was Peter’s interpreter and wrote down accurately what Peter remembered of the Lord. His Gospel is vivid and urgent, full of the word ‘immediately’, and shows the disciples’ failures plainly. Some think he was the young man who fled naked from Gethsemane. Tradition says he was martyred at Alexandria.
prayerTo: Saint Mark, you once turned back from the work, and by God’s grace became useful for His service and wrote the Good News of Jesus Christ. Pray for all who have failed and been given a second chance, and for me, that I may follow Christ without turning back. Amen.
penance: Read the Gospel of Mark today, or as much of it as you can; it takes about two hours to read aloud. Be reconciled with someone you have fallen out with.
meditation: Paul once refused to take him; later he called him useful. Is there someone you have written off whom God has not?
